tasks.short: Transmit medical records or correspondence by mail or fax.

steps.what: Collect the medical records the request names.

loop.input: The request and the chart index
loop.output: The named documents, and a list of names the request left unclear
loop.check: Secretary opens each selected document and checks the patient identity
loop.stop: One pass; an unclear name is not included
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests name records in prose, not by a stable identifier

steps.what: Decide whether that recipient may receive the records.
Prepare the pack and the short cover note.

loop.input: The accepted documents and the recipient
loop.output: A cover note that lists only those documents
loop.check: Secretary checks the note lists no extra document
loop.stop: One draft; a document not in the pack is deleted from the note
loop.why_not_simpler: The note must follow this request, which is not a stored paragraph

steps.what: Transmit the approved records by mail or fax.
Log the disclosure on the patient's chart.

tasks.design: The chart index proposes the documents named in the request. The secretary decides whether that recipient may have them, checks the cover note, and only then is the pack sent. The disclosure is written on the chart. Native chart search is tested before custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were photocopied from a paper file and faxed from memory of who was allowed to ask.
tasks.enabler_now: The chart index can list document titles. The right to receive them is still a person.
tasks.still_hard: Requests that name a family member, an insurer and a lawyer in one note.
tasks.human_edge: The secretary knows which request is a real authority to release the file.

ambition.what: The secretary decides, before anything is sent, whether this recipient is allowed to receive this pack.

tasks.altitude: Release decisions stay on the week. The secretary can stop a pack that names the wrong patient or the wrong recipient.

reach.task: Release a case file only to a named recipient
reach.learn: Which proof of identity they require before a copy leaves

evidence.claim: A chart index can list documents. Choosing the recipient is a person.
Health data is a special category under GDPR article 9.
The file is confidential under the WGBO and is kept for the statutory period.
A Dutch GP-practice employee who pasted medical data into a free chatbot was treated as a breach. This design stays inside the record system.

assumptions: Focal role is the medical secretary. Boundary: from a request for records to a logged transmission. Deciding a legal dispute about access is out of scope.

Structured fields are patient identifier, document identifiers, recipient name and channel. The requester names the documents. Fallback: the secretary pulls a document the index missed and refuses an unclear recipient.
Test the record system's own send or download before custom code. The pack is not pasted into a free chatbot.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers the recipient checklist when the practice updates who may receive a file.
unknowns: Who is allowed to authorise a release in this practice.
Whether fax is still used or every pack is a secure mail.
research_questions: What share of requests is missing a clear authority to release?

already_counted.description: Check the documents the index selected

incremental.description: Revise the recipient checklist when release rules change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most requests are unclear, so the secretary still pulls the file by hand and the send stays manual. High: the index finds the documents and only the recipient decision and the note check remain. The release decision is not removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain medical records, the technical library and correspondence files.

steps.what: File incoming medical records under the right heading.

loop.input: The document title, patient identifiers and the library headings
loop.output: A proposed patient or library heading, or unmatched
loop.check: Secretary opens the document and confirms the patient or the heading
loop.stop: One pass; unmatched documents go to a review queue
loop.why_not_simpler: Titles and scanned covers do not follow one naming rule

steps.what: Apply the retention date from the file rule.
Review a duplicate chart or a record marked for destruction.
Approve or refuse destruction of that record.
Remove the approved record from the active file.

tasks.design: Incoming documents are proposed for a patient or a library heading, and the secretary confirms the match. Retention dates come from the file rule in the record system. Nothing is destroyed unless the practice manager has approved that record. Native filing rules are tested before custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing was a shelf and a spelling of the patient's name. Retention lived on a paper list.
tasks.enabler_now: Identifiers and a retention rule can stamp a date and propose a heading. Merging two charts is still a person.
tasks.still_hard: Two patients with the same name, and library items that are not a patient record.
tasks.human_edge: The secretary can see that two charts are the same person, or that they are not.
tasks.altitude: Filing stays on the week, but less of it is retyping a heading. The secretary can refuse to merge a chart the match got wrong.

reach.task: File and weed a technical collection
reach.learn: How they separate a duplicate from a new edition

evidence.claim: A record system can file on an identifier and stamp a retention date. A person still merges or destroys a chart.
The medical file is kept for the WGBO period. A destruction shorter than that period is not this design.

assumptions: Focal role is the medical secretary. Boundary: from an incoming document or a retention sweep to a filed, dated or destroyed record. Clinical content is not edited here.

Structured fields are patient identifier, document type, library heading and retention class. The sender produces the document. The practice sets the retention class. Fallback: unmatched items stay in a queue for the secretary.
Test native filing and retention configuration before custom code. Destruction is a separate approved step, not the daily file.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers headings and retention classes.
unknowns: Whether the practice already stores a patient identifier on every scan.
research_questions: What share of incoming documents lacks a patient identifier?

incremental.description: Update headings and retention classes when the file rule changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most documents have no identifier, so filing stays manual, and destruction candidates are rare. High: headings match and only duplicate review remains. Destruction does not run unattended.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive laboratory results and route them to the right staff.

steps.what: Retype laboratory results that already arrived structured.
Route a normal result to the ordering staff by the panel rule.
Read an out-of-range or unmatched laboratory result.
Call the clinician about a critical result.

tasks.design: Structured laboratory results land in the record system and a panel rule routes the normal ones to the ordering staff. The secretary still reads an out-of-range or unmatched result and telephones a critical value. The retype step goes away. Native routing is tested before custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results arrived as paper or a portal printout and were retyped, then walked to a tray.
tasks.enabler_now: A structured result and a panel rule can route the normal cases. A critical value is still a phone call.
tasks.still_hard: Results with no order number, and values that are odd for this patient but inside the lab range.
tasks.human_edge: The secretary knows which odd value can wait in a tray and which one cannot.

ambition.what: The secretary decides, as the result arrives, whether it is a phone call or a routed file.

tasks.altitude: Critical calls stay on the week. The secretary can pull a result off the automatic route.

reach.task: Decide which incoming message is urgent
reach.learn: How they separate a routine message from one that must be spoken now

evidence.claim: Structured laboratory results can be routed by a panel rule. A person still handles the result that does not match.
A filed result is part of the medical file under the WGBO.

assumptions: Focal role is the medical secretary. Boundary: from a result arriving to a route or a phone call. Interpreting the result clinically is the clinician's work.

Structured fields are order number, patient identifier, test code and numeric value. The laboratory produces them. Fallback: an unmatched result stays in the secretary's queue and is not guessed onto a chart.
Test the record system's own result interface and route before custom code. No result is pasted into a free chatbot.
Upkeep of 3 hours per 100 baseline hours covers panel rules when the laboratory changes a code.
unknowns: Whether this laboratory already sends a structured result or a PDF.
Which values the practice treats as a phone call.
research_questions: What share of results arrives without an order number?

incremental.description: Update panel routes when a laboratory code changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most results are PDFs or unmatched, so the secretary still reads and routes them by hand. High: normal panels route themselves and only out-of-range results and phone calls remain. The critical call is not removed.

tasks.short: Interview patients and complete intake or insurance forms.

steps.what: Open the intake or insurance form for this visit.
Interview patients and write the history answers.
Read the answers into the intake form fields.

loop.output: Intake fields, blank where the note is silent
loop.check: Secretary reads each field back against the note
loop.stop: One pass; a silent field is left blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients answer in sentences, not in the form's boxes

steps.what: Check the form with the patient and ask for a signature.
Sign the intake or insurance form.

tasks.design: The record system opens the intake or insurance form for the visit. The secretary still interviews the patient and writes the answers. Those notes fill the fields, the secretary reads them back, and only that version is put forward for signature. Native form configuration is tested first.
tasks.previous_blocker: The form was paper, filled during the conversation, and later retyped into the chart.
tasks.enabler_now: The form fields exist, so the retype can follow the notes. The interview cannot be skipped.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who do not know the answer, and forms that ask for a clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The secretary notices when an answer does not match the person in the chair.
tasks.altitude: Interviews stay on the week. The secretary can refuse to request a signature on a form they have not read back.

reach.task: Interview a person to complete an application
reach.learn: Which questions they ask aloud when the person cannot fill the form

evidence.claim: An interview that collects a history stays with a person. Form fields can be filled from that person's notes afterwards.
Intake answers about health are special-category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Focal role is the medical secretary. Boundary: from opening the form to a signed intake. Diagnosis is out of scope.
Structured fields are identity, cover, allergies and the answers the form already lists. The patient supplies them in the interview. Fallback: a field the note does not support stays blank.
Test the native intake form before custom code. The model does not interview the patient.
Upkeep of 3 hours per 100 baseline hours covers form revisions.
The prior that this task vanishes is rejected: the interview is the work.
unknowns: Whether patients can complete any fields before they arrive.
research_questions: What share of intake answers is already on a previous visit?

already_counted.description: Reading fields back to the notes
Checking the form and requesting the signature

incremental.description: Update intake and insurance form fields when the blank form changes

approvals.approved_version: intake version the secretary read back to the patient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the interview is the whole task and the notes do not map to the form, so little changes. High: the form opens itself and the retype shrinks, while the interview and the read-back stay. The conversation is not removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the phone, the front door and the desk. Standard bookings, bills and chart packs are ready to check. The secretary can refuse to file or send a record that failed the identity or recipient check.
reach: Eligibility interviewers: which intake questions must be asked aloud
Court clerks: which identity check they require before a copy leaves
Hotel desk clerks: how a busy desk looks up a name without losing the queue
skills_to_grow: Reading a clinical term before it is filed
Maintaining a booking rule and a prep line
Spotting a result that must be phoned, not routed
role.ambitious_version: Every result has an owner, every disclosure names the recipient, and no chart line is filed before a person has read it.
